alignments.note: Inflected verb takes its supplied subject and auxiliary; rule 9 heads on the lexical verb *loved*.
Anarthrous abstract noun, no determiner supplied.
The ASV does not repeat the auxiliary; the verb stands on its own English word.

Rule 45: preposition plus governed demonstrative rendered by a single English word answering to neither token separately, exactly as `διὰ τοῦτο` → *wherefore* is recorded; headed on the governed demonstrative. Rule 81 is not the case, *Therefore* being no *here-*/*there-* portmanteau spelling either element.
Rule 9: auxiliary rides with the verb, headed on the lexical *anointed*.
Rule 23: the ASV writes a bare *God* for the first subject, so this article has no English realization.
Rule 20: the genitive `σου` is present and free to carry the possessive *thy*, so the article governing the second `θεός` is displaced and realizes nothing.
Rule 20: the genitive pronoun carries the possessive.

The Greek is anarthrous, so under rule 51's anarthrous clause the supplied *the* is a rule 7 helper on the noun, and the case preposition *With* rides with it since no article stands to anchor it (rules 21, 23).
Rule 17: a source noun rendered *of + noun* heads on the noun.
Rule 20: `σου` occupies the determiner slot as *thy*, so this article realizes nothing.
Rule 20: genitive pronoun takes the possessive.

review_notes: Two of the three articles are emptied by a following genitive pronoun under rule 20; the first (s010) is emptied by rule 23, the ASV writing a bare *God*.

`διὰ τοῦτο` → *Therefore* is taken as rule 45's noncompositional pair. Splitting *Therefore* is impossible and giving it to the demonstrative alone would leave the preposition unrepresented, which rule 45 forbids by name.
`ἔλαιον` is anarthrous, so *the* is a helper on the noun rather than evidence of an article; rule 58's determiner-on-the-noun reasoning points the same way.
